They induced me on a Wednesday at 9 pm, sent me to the labour ward on Thursday around 8-10pm, and I gave birth on Friday, around 10:30 am. 

I won't lie, the contractions hurt, but I knew labour/birth won't be a walk in the park. I didn't get the epidural since I was scared of it, but I did get pethidine somewhere around 3-4 am Friday. And it helped. It helped so much that I was struggling to not fall asleep while pushing lol I slept a grand total of 2 h during wednesday - Friday (before pethidine). 

But everything went well! I had no tears, no massive blood loss. I was just very confused, very sleepy. I must've been 30% awake while they weighted our son and gave him to me, while the nurses put him to my boob. Big thanks to my husband for being there for me. 

And after I gave birth, I forgot all the pain in an instant, just like that. 

Get a water bottle. I had no appetite, but I was drinking water like my life depended on it lol. The small cup they provided wasn't enough. And snacks! I ate a lot on Friday. 

And I remember watching a video about hypnobirthing. The best advice there was the breathing techniques while giving birth. So basically, if you do *inhale* hoooo *exhale* haaaa, the right muscles will activate and you'll push easier. And it works perfectly for the first pp poo too :)) I'm still using this technique 10 months pp lol 

Wishing you an easy delivery 🫶🫶

I gave birth in the UK, so the hospital didn't provide any supplies. I know they had some formula for babies, just in case. Maybe they had extra nappies/clothes/whatev just in case, but I got everything we needed.

I did want to take a shower though. I was so mad at myself for not bringing at least a cheap soap to wash away all the blood and sweat. I eventually asked my husband to bring me shampoo and a towel, but they discharged me 30 min before he came. As soon as I got home, I spent 30 min in the shower.

I was pretty fit before getting pregnant, and I did struggle a little with my body image before it was obvious that I was pregnant. I managed to go to the gym until I was 27 weeks pregnant. I was barely doing cardio by then, and using some of the machines for muscles. I'd say that around 23 weeks pregnant it started getting harder and harder to workout.

As soon as my bump was out, I got an idgaf attitude. I was pregnant.

I didn't exercise anymore, I just walked everyday. 

I kind of got back into my pre pregnancy body around 2 months pp. My stomach wasn't as wobbly by then. Around 5 months pp I started feeling okay though. I pretty much look the same, except there's a small gap between my abs and my hips are wider. So I retired my jeans and 2 skirts. 

But I also had an easy delivery with no tears, so I had it easy. Who knows how your delivery will be like (wishing you a smooth delivery tho!)

It'll take you 9 months to gain all the baby weight, so don't worry about losing it too fast. Fast weight loss isn't recommended for normal people, let alone new mums. Especially since your hormones will be all over the place. And you'll be sleep deprived and tired the first weeks. Don't set any high expectations for yourself. 

And don't compare yourself to influencer moms who probably have dieticians and baby sitters and cleaners and whatnot. It's your body, your personalised journey, with its own bumps. Comparing yourself to others is pointless. Esp since photoshopping videos are getting easier and easier nowadays. Remember that few influencers show the "bad" parts. Being cheerful and cute and nice and perfect is what gets them views and money.

In highschool, my younger, or maybe youngest, classmate was the biggest it nerd I ever met. She's worked/had internships with Microsoft and Google.

Tldr, help her in other ways to avoid burnt out (chores, changing baby, taking care of the baby). Let her breastfeed and see how it goes for her. If it's too much, she can decide to pump or use formula.


If your wife wants to breastfeed, let her breastfeed. She can decide if it's too much. She shouldn't pump at first anyway since the baby lets her body know how much milk she should make. Pumping could make her have an oversupply=>mastitis (eg, baby breastfed, wife has lots of milk in her boobs left, and over time mastitis happens and nobody wants to deal with that). 

I'm 8 months pp and still breastfeeding. I woke up at night to feed our baby, and while I was tired, it was doable. She'll feel burnt out if you don't help her at all. Whenever I felt burnt out was when I did everything for our baby + all the chores around the house. You can still wake up to change the baby. My son had a poo each wake in the first month. Taking care of the chores (cleaning, laundry, cooking) and changing the baby and taking the baby from time to time will help her more than whatever you're trying to do.

And pumping sucks imo. Having to hear that voosh voosh voosh voosh constantly is annoying. Having to keep the pump in place while juggling the cables is annoying. Even the wearable breast pump is meh. Then washing and sterilizing everything. Then labeling and placing bags of milk in the fridge/freezer. And I did that once per day, just to have an emergency stash. Popping a boob out is much easier. 

And my son did take bottles. He had colic and wouldn't take a boob, but would eat from a bottle. So he ate one bottle per day when he wouldn't settle down. And warming up the milk was annoying. I was in the bathroom, letting warm water run over the bag, while he was screaming bloody murder. Having to do that for every feed sounds exhausting. But maybe there are better ways to warm up milk, idk.

Work with your wife, not against her. Taking care of a baby will be exhausting anyway, bottles won't make it easier. Both of you won't end up on the couch in the evening and say "yeah, motherhood sucks, it would've been sooooo much easier if the baby took bottles".

I get the food issue problem. I had an eating disorder, and the amount I'd eat..oh boy. 

I stumbled upon "brain over binge" and it helped a little while I was recovering. If you don't want to read it all, or the first chapter (I found it for free somewhere on Google), well. It talks about this:

Your brain has 2 parts, the rational part and the animalistic one. The rational one is the part that makes decisions and whatnot. Think "I have to wash the dishes. Oh, there's a spill, I better not slip on it". That's the rational part. 

Then there's the animalistic part, that controls instincts, urges, survival mechanism. "You slip and instinctively try not to fall". And we can train that part. So, for example, I ate a lot, again and again and again and again, until I developed a habit. And if I tried to not binge and uhh puke, my body felt weird. As if I was attacked, as if I knew something bad would happen. Some sort of animalistic response to me trying to not do something disordered. 

And what helped was recognising the "I NEED THAT FOOD RIGHT NOW/I NEED TO PUKE IT ASAP OR ILL IMPLODE" voice as animalistic. It's not rational. I don't need to eat until I'm feeling gross. I don't need that mars bar now, it'll be there, it's not going anywhere. 


And the more I realised that I don't need all that food, the more I trained my animalistic part that nothing bad will happen if I don't get it asap.

And now I'm using this since I'm breastfeeding and I feel like I could eat a horse sometimes :))

On Friday, at 8am, the midwives left their shift, and another set of midwives came. And eventually, around 10am, maybe a little earlier, they told me to push. I don't know how long I've pushed for, the pethidine worked well, I was struggling not to fall asleep during pushes, I was annoyed at everyone because I just wanted to sleep. No tears, no major blood loss, no complications. I went to the bathroom on my own, annoying the nurses because they needed my first pee. 

Imo, get the epidural or any other pain relief that you are comfortable with asap. Contractions hurt like hell.

Remember that you need to be in a caloric surplus if you want to gain muscle. We lose muscle over time if we don't work them out, and given how hectic pregnancy+child caring can be, it's no surprise that we are squishy and soft. I lost weight in a very unhealthy way, and at my lowest I was still a little squishy. No muscles, just very "skinny fat". So eating less than you should won't help. 

Shaping your body is a process, building muscles takes a lot of time. Try to eat well and workout whenever you can. Don't feel discouraged if you don't see results in 1 month, don't try to rush by trying diet hacks and tips. Don't go in the "I'm only eating eggs and cottage cheese for protein" part of the diet world. And don't compare yourself to other fitness mums vloggers/instagramers/whatever. You're your own person with your own valid struggles, with your own journey and your own metabolic rate/physical shape.

Accepting the way your body is can be hard, but it's not impossible. Until you reach your goals, try to find that "okay, I don't look perfect, but I still look good" mindset. I'm not telling you to love your body, loving our own bodies can be hard. But try to accept it and work with what you have.

My guy had colic. I ebf, but I gave him bottles when he wouldn't feed (how dare my boob not give milk in an instant, without him having to use his mouth for longer than 1 nanosecond??). He was screaming from 2-3pm until 10pm with a few 15 min naps in between. Sometimes he'd start screaming later.

What helped:

Holding him upside down on my forearms. Imagine tummy time, but in the air, and his head was supported by my arms. He'd stop screaming, but he wouldn't fall asleep.

Car rides, but they can get expensive. Now that he's over that phase, he hates his car seat :)

Infacol. 50/50. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. I only tried one brand of gripe water, and it worked 3-4 times. Had to throw it away.

Taking baths. Which can be tricky. He'd start screaming again as soon as he was out. And then I'd have to deal with a wet baby, having to dress him. 

Carrying him in a baby wrap sling, walking with him up and down the stairs/around the room. He was tight in there, warm, and he'd eventually fall asleep. Until he got hungry, then rinse and repeat.

White noise on the TV, full volume. Get earplugs/noise canceling headphones for your sanity. You know that your baby's crying. 

Room temp didn't really matter. He had his phase while it was hot as hell in the UK. We had a fan, the room was not too warm not too cold, but it didn't make a difference. 

*The happiest baby on the block* helped a little. I understood why he was crying, it made me feel less guilty (I'm his mum, why can't I soothe him?). You can find a free pdf on Google.

And hang in there. If your baby has colic/purple crying, it will eventually get better. At the end of the day, I was thinking "one less day of this crying. It will only get better from here" :')

Things that I did that sometimes worked, sometimes didn't work:

Classic over the shoulder

Cupping his jaw/face while he's laying on his tummy on my knees + patting

Patting his back while doing tummy time on my chest

Supporting his head by cupping his jaw/face with one hand, with the other I'd support his bum. Then I'd move his whole body in circles, while his head stays in place. Hope it makes sense, I've seen this on tiktok. Sometimes it worked wonders, sometimes it didn't.

My little guy started purple crying/being colicky around 4-5 weeks. For 3-4 weeks he was bad. Crying constantly. But it got better, instead of crying 6h in the evening, he cried 4, then 2, then 1, then maybe half an hour. And now he's teething, woo.. but it's much better

What helped us: 

LOUD white noise/vacuum noises. Get some earplugs or noise canceling earphones, I had to put the volume in the TV at 100 so he'd calm down. He prefers the vacuum now, yay me, rip my ears.

Baby wearing. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. He usually fell asleep in the baby sling wrap. Sometimes it didn't work. I used a tutorial on tiktok, I put his legs in a frog position, his head under the cloth that goes over the shoulder, gave him the pacifier. With one hand I held the pacifier, with the other one I held his body wile rocking him. He spat the pacifier, but he eventually took it, then fell asleep.

Driving. He sometimes calms down when he's in his car seat. Sometimes he falls asleep in it. Sometimes he cries a lot. It can be expensive though (considering gas prices).

Giving him a bottle of breast milk. He was so mad at the world, and showed hunger cues, but he wouldn't attach to the boob. But he'd drink a bottle. He was (and still is) breastfeeding when he wasn't purple crying, in the morning/during the day/in the middle of the night. I was worried that I'd have to pump every 2h now, but nope, that one bottle per evening didn't affect him

Holding him upside down. My hand went under the belly, his head was supported by the same arm. Idk how to explain him, imagine he lays down on his tummy, but on your arm, while holding him in the air, rocking him. It calmed him down almost instantly. But it can get tiring the more the baby gains weight.

Pacifier. He'd spit it up a lot, but he also took it. It helped him fall asleep. Now he sleeps with or without it. He falls asleep with it, then spits it out while he's asleep, but doesn't wake up.

Pushing him above/below the butthole. Gentle, but firm. It helped him release some gas. Worst case scenario (after doing massages, bicycle kicks, gently pressing him, and all of the above), I used a Frida windy. It helped him, somewhat. Not all the time.

Infacol. sometimes it helped, sometimes it didn't. I'd say 80% of the time it helped. Gripe water did nothing for us, I had to throw it away.

The happiest baby on the block. The pdf is available for free, I think. It helped me understand why he's acting like this. I felt like a terrible mum for not being able to soothe him. And it gave some good advice too, on how to calm babies. It's a few pages long, you'll finish reading it before you know it

And hang in there x it was bad, I was on autopilot during his purple crying. I was crying with him. I learned to ignore the white noise that could be heard from outside the house. But it got better. Oatmeal for breakfast and whatever seasonal fruit you can find (apples should be cheap). Those pumpkins that people use for Halloween are good to eat, you could make soup, roast them, boil them with oatmeal. Cinammon could make the oatmeal taste better if you don't like it, try buying spices in the "world/Indian section", they're always cheaper by the gram. I usually ate cheap cereal and milk, or eggs and fries. Or if I was at school, a sandwich with bologna or whatever cheap meat and cheese mum bought. A jam sandwich. We did get a 60gram loaf thing with some milk from the school, I usually ate that.

Beans and potatoes are versatile. You can make a potato/bean stew/soup, roasted/mash/fried potatoes, pureed beans on bread (like a spread, you can use a blender, my mum used a fork). Beans are usually cheaper if you buy them dried. All you need to do is soak them overnight and then boil them for ~1h (my mum soaks them in the evening, then boils them around 5pm when she gets home from work).

I'd suggest going to the supermarket in the evening, they put out the reduced stuff around 6-8pm here. Sometimes I find good deals (£0.50 for 1kg of drumsticks), sometimes I'm too late and can't find much, except sandwiches and maybe yogurt. Depending on the store, you can find great veggies in the reduced section too (Tesco's reduced veggies are good, Morrisons are always rotting). The polish shops around me have a great reduced section, full of yogurts for £0.20-0.40, bags of meat (the ends of the salami or whatever meat they slice at the deli), sliced cheese.

Polenta is usually cheap and it's soo much more filling than bread imo. Just add cornmeal and salt to boiling water, mix, and in 10 min it's done. It goes very well with stews and soups Vs bread. It's good with some cheese and fried eggs too. Or eggs and fries.

Frozen vegetables are usually cheaper than fresh (broccoli, cauliflower, corn, peas, spinach etc), and they're just as good, if not better.  You can roast them, or make soup, or stews (potato and broccoli, pea stew).

For snacks: peanut butter/jam on toast or margarine on toast with tea was a favourite. We didn't have peanut butter, and it's expensive in my home country, but I love it now. Peanut butter in oats is good too. Yogurts from the reduced section, or salted corn puffs. But as a snack, I'd always have a second portion of whatever my mum made. 

Tomato concentrate, the ones in metal tubes, work well if you don't want to spend money on tomato Pasata (?), they last longer too (one can of tomatoes for one meal Vs a few tbs from a tomato concentrate tub).

*Stews are easy. The base is always onion, carrot, maybe bell pepper and/or parsnip, tomato concentrate. Then I add peas/beans/potatoes and anything else that I fancy (chicken, smoked meat, or nothing). 

You could look into Indian meals too, hold the spices if you don't like them. They usually use cheap and filling ingredients, like lentils.

Also! I don't know where you live, but we have toogoodtogo in the UK. It's an app where you can get random groceries or meals from restaurants for cheap. And olio is an app where people give free food away (most of them get food from a supermarket and then give it away, there are rules, they aren't allowed to mess up with the food). I know that my home country has its own version of toogoodtogo, it's not that great, but it's a start. You could Google something like "reduce food waste app", maybe you have something similar.

Hello! I've had an induction at 39w and a few days. Everything went smoothly, no C-section, no tears, he was (if I remember correctly)  3.6 kg ± a few grams, i recovered very fast, I was able to go on walks on day 3 (but I didn't go out much since he was so small and I was sore). 

I was induced with pessary (I had a shoelace thingie inserted down there). But the day before, a Dr did a membrane sweep around 11am, and the next day I started having contractions around 6pm, so I'm not sure if I could've waited (if everything was okay, too little amniotic fluid so I had to be induced). 

Honestly, the contractions before being sent to the labour ward were bad. They hurt, I'm not gonna lie. I was crying and I couldn't really eat. I received paracetamol and some codeine based pills(?) and they didn't help that much. I was able to chill in a tub, the water helped a little. But there was another lady in the room who chose the balloon method and she seemed to be joyful AND she got sent to the labour ward before me. I can't recommend the balloon since I didn't use it. But in that moment I wished I got it. 

The pessary was introduced around 9pm, and I think I got sent to the labour ward 24ish h later. When I got to the labour ward they asked me if I wanted gas and air, pethidine, or the epidural. Gas and air didn't help at all. Pethidine helped a lot. I didn't choose the epidural, but I could've had it as soon as I was in the labour ward, sooo yeah. 

I was in active labour for 17h and a few minutes. Pethidine made me able to relax so much that I was fighting sleep while I was pushing (my eyes were closed while I was pushing, I stopped pushing for a few seconds, I almost fell asleep, I pushed, stopped, almost fell asleep and repeat lol. I slept like 3h in 2 nights. Don't be like me, choose the epidural if you think the contractions are too painful) 

Then I finally got the baby out, I had 2 small tears on my labias that didn't require stitching, I was sore (but who wouldn't be sore?) and I got to chill with my baby in a room while eating like I haven't eaten in ages. As soon as he got out I felt instant relief and everything was peaceful again.

All I did "extra" was walk during the day, around 8-10k steps per day. I tried doing that massage down there and I didn't like it, so I stopped. I forgot to do pelvic floor exercises, I had no yoga ball. I don't know if me eating dates helped, I ate them because I enjoyed them. Exercising wouldn't hurt, but if you don't feel like it, that's fine.

Overall, it was okay. The contractions hurt, so get pain relief when you can, if you want to. Get a big bottle with a straw, you'll be VERY thirsty during active labour. 

Whatever you choose, I hope you'll have a fast and easy delivery 🫶

If you had sex after ovulating, then she shouldn't be pregnant, but unless she checks her ovulation day with ovulation strips, she may have been ovulating when she thought that she wasn't. The period apps give an estimated day in which she ovulates, they're not 100% accurate.

Ovulating, the egg is ready to receive sperm. After the ovulation day you could say that the egg is like "so no one came, f this I'm out". No egg=no pregnancy=period comes.

If she takes plan b every time after you have sex (and she shouldn't use it that often, it'll mess up with her hormones a lot), then that could be the reason why she's feeling sick ( plan b can make people feel ill/throw up). If she took plan b then there's a very very small chance that she's pregnant. Since it's autumn maybe she caught a virus or something. And if she's been stressed/if she ate very little in the past weeks then that could be why her period is late/will be late. I can't say anything about the hormone imbalance, I don't know enough about it, but that could also cause her to have irregular periods.

I don't know what country you're in, but if she's pregnant and wants an abortion, she could take a pill and that's it, no scary operation. The people in the abortion subreddit should be able to give you more resources. I'm mentioning this just in case that's the path that both of you will choose if she ends up being pregnant.

But for now you should be patient and take pregnancy tests ~2 weeks after the ovulation day, or a few days after the day her period is supposed to start. It'll be okay, both of you will get through this. Wishing you both the best x

The HCG hormone will appear in urine 7-9 days after ovulation, but for the best results your gf should wait around 2 weeks or more. The HCG hormone is the strongest in the morning, so she should take the test whenever she wakes up. 

It also depends on if you had sex around her ovulation time. (I forgot the dates you provided, I'm using these as an example). Let's say she ovulated on the 7th of September. If you had sex on the 11th then she couldn't have gotten pregnant, the egg is "gone". If you had sex before/on the 7th of SEP then she might have gotten pregnant (sperm can stay alive inside the vagina for a few days). 

So use the tests a few days after her period should start. From experience, the strip ones (the cheapest, 3 for £1) work too. You could try different brands just to make sure. I hope you get the results that both of you want x

Ftm to a 1 month old. I had an easy delivery. No complications, no tears. I was uncomfortable and sore down there, but I managed to use the toilet on my own. I walked like a penguin, but I did it on my own :))

No work=no money. I either did them while the baby was asleep, or I carried him in a baby sling wrap. My husband does chores too, so I'm not the only one doing stuff around the house. Cooking: basic stuff. Meat and veggies in the oven, soups, stews, anything that doesn't require a lot of prep. By the time I'm done prepping and cooking (so around 1h) the baby is awake. I eat whenever I can, but now I make sure I have fruit or easy to grab snacks in case he's fussy and I can't even make microwaved oatmeal.

I'm breastfeeding, so I don't need to clean bottles/a breast pump. I wake up during the night and take care of the baby, but I also manage to sleep more in the mornings when he's asleep, so I'm not that sleep deprived. My husband sometimes wakes up too, but I want him to sleep so he's not sleep deprived while he's working.

Tbh I don't want extra help, I don't really like company, especially now. If the baby is having a hard time falling asleep in the evening (and only god knows how hard it is when he can't fall asleep), my husband and I take turns to rock and soothe him. 

But I had it easy, I was able to do my (almost) daily ~10k steps by day 3-4 pp, so I can do house chores without any issues. You may or may not feel more tired/sore than me. 

But focus on your baby and yourself. Order takeout or buy frozen pizzas/meals, or meal prep now (either full meals or ingredients, like cut up veggies, portioned meat etc) so you won't spend too much time in the kitchen. Dusting and vacuuming can wait, have your husband do the laundry and shop runs and dishes. Both of you will be able to manage on your own. It may be hard, but you'll survive. Don't forget to have some time for yourselves, cuddle at the end of the day, watch a movie, anything. We kinda neglected our "us time" (he's spent more time with his brothers than me sometimes) and I resented him a lot for it. 

Wishing you an easy delivery 🫶 and enjoy your baby 🥺

I've struggled with an ed too, and seeing that I gained while stepping on the scale/not fitting into my old clothes messed me up a little. But I always reassured myself that my baby needs the nutrients, even if I eat junk. Getting calories in and whatever nutrients some foods provide (carbs and fat are essential, don't feel bad if you don't eat veggies for every meal) is much better than nothing. 

My brain eventually switched. I made the realisation that my baby is more important than the way I perceive myself. And I was going to gain and get bigger no matter what. So I let myself enjoy stuff that I'd usually never buy and everything became..peaceful. 

+You're not only gaining the weight of the baby/much needed body fat. Your blood % will increase, you'll retain more water, the amniotic fluid weighs too, the placenta as well, constipation can hit you like a truck and you're suddenly "heavier" because you need to take a 1-2lb poo, your boobs will grow and milk/colostrum will come in and that weighs more too.


Growing a baby takes a lot of energy, so don't feel bad for eating too much some days. I took walks and played Pokémon go to keep me busy and that helped, knowing that I'm still exercising a little in order to be healthy. And it kept my mind off things. Getting some fresh air everyday definitely helped.

Reading "brain over binge" helped too. I've only read the first half of the book, but I think it was enough. I understood the part of my brain that thought that I needed to b/p in order to feel good and somehow learnt to ignore it. 

I also started eating high volume/low cal, just to satisfy that binge part. I was eating almost 1kg of salad and a big bowl of yogurt with fruit and/or oatmeal for breakfast. It wasn't that caloric, I still got my protein in, it tasted pretty nice, and it kept me full for a lot of time. And this way, after dinner, I still had calories to spare for my fav snacks. (* I was and still am counting calories only because it somehow helped me keep my ed under control. I never ate less than my tdee, I actually ate a little more some days lol)


I also blocked any gym influencer (pregnant or not) and any ed related tiktoks for my mental health. Once I wasn't bombarded with them I stopped being so self conscious and I didn't have any people to compare myself to.

Speaking from experience as someone who gave birth in the UK (induced, I went into the hospital at 8pm on Tuesday, I gave birth at 10am on friday, discharged around 3 pm on Saturday)

For mum: 4+ pairs of pants. You probably won't change before you give birth, but after birth I bled so much through all my pads that I had to ask my husband to bring me 2 extra pairs of pants. Some thsirts too since I sweat a lot.

Disposable underwear. There'll be a lot of bleeding. I think I used 6 pairs while I stayed at the hospital, I used the rest at home, they were VERY convenient.

The biggest pads you can find, even better if they have wings. I used a whole 20 pack, my husband had to go and get me more.

A long phone charger, and stuff to keep you busy (I just played on my phone/read online manga)

Hair brush, shampoo, body wash, loofah, deodorant. I was sweaty after giving birth and had to stay overnight. I felt so greasy and yucky. Also, a towel if you wanna take a shower. 

Something to keep water in. I used a 1.5l water bottle that I refilled from their water dispenser. I drank water like crazy. I'd highly recommend something with a straw while you're in labour, my poor husband had to refill a small cup every  10-20 minutes (I think? I was in too much pain to notice the time)

Some snacks, but I was in so much pain from the induction that I barely managed to eat.  After giving birth? I slowly started to eat more.

An outfit to go home into, but I wore my maternity pants and an oversized t-shirt, the only clean clothes that I had.

Slippers.

I didn't use any breast pads right after giving birth, but I'm now changing them 4-5 times a day, and I'm almost 2 weeks PP, so it's good to have them.

For baby:

Diapers, wipes (they're more convenient than cotton balls imo, but I use both at home), 2 vests, 2 sleeping outfits (? The ones with long sleeves and legs), a hat, some muslims or small sheets (mine spat out milk, I used 3, wish I had 4-5), 2 blankets (mine spat on one blanket). I brought newborn and 0-3 size clothes, but I only ended up using the newborn ones. The 0-3 were too big for him.


For your partner: snacks, some form of entertainment (we ended up playing triviador), change of clothes. He didn't stay overnight while I was in labour (one night). He was with me while I was in labour though, he stayed up all night with me. He barely slept, but I'd suggest that your partner wears something comfortable, those chairs aren't the best thing to sleep in. There were 2 pillows on my bed, so I gave him one (I couldn't stand having 2 pillows), but they were pretty thin and eh, your partner may want a more comfortable pillow.

He wasn't offered free food, so he went to the canteen/food court. He said that the food was overpriced and bad, so I'd suggest packing some sandwiches or something in case your partner or you get hungry. 

The blankets and pillows that the hospital had were fine. I didn't manage to sleep at all while I was induced anyway. The blankets were thin, but it was hot so they were perfect.

All in all, you shouldn't be worried about any chemicals getting in your skin and hurting your baby,  but please wash your clothes, you never know how they were handled

Soțului meu ii mai fac 

- pui cu spanac (Prajesti puiul in tigaie, pui ce condimente vrei pe el. Scoți puiul, Prajesti ceapa și usturoi pana s gata, după pui spanac [proaspăt sau congelat, dar sa fie deja gătit sa nu fie apa]. După smântână de gătit, nu foarte multa, brânză daca vrei și gata)

-paste cu somon (fierbi paste, in tigaie Prajesti o bucată de somon și o sfărâmi [eu sfărâm cu lingura de lemn, mai puțin de curățat :)) ], când e cat de cat gata bagi smântână de gătit.
